paras: The killing of John Rhodes was the shooting of a Black man in his cabin on the Carson place, near Friars Point, Mississippi, by two masked men on a Saturday night in late 1881, probably December 3. Rhodes died of a shot to the head, and the only report supposed that the men had meant not to kill him but to frighten him off the place.

According to the report, Rhodes, described as "a colored man," lived on the Carson place near Friars Point. On what the item called "last Saturday night," two masked men came to his cabin and shot him in the head, killing him. The men were not named, and their race was not given. The item offered a motive only as a supposition: "it was not the intention to kill him, but merely to frighten him off the place."
No report of an arrest, an inquest or any official response appears in the coverage.

The killing reached print as a single paragraph in the Jackson Weekly Clarion of December 7, 1881, in a column of "Mississippi Items" that the paper said was "condensed from our exchanges." Because the original exchange was not named, the "last Saturday" of the item cannot be fixed with certainty, though December 3 is the Saturday before the Clarion's issue. The paragraph stood without a headline among notices of deaths, marriages, a jail escape and railroad news, and it neither condemned the killing nor named any suspect. Its closing line treated the death as an unintended result of an effort to drive Rhodes away rather than as a murder.
No other report of the killing appears in the coverage.
